facts.statement: Coahomasuchus is an extinct genus belonging to the aetosaurine group of aetosaurs.
facts.quote: Coahomasuchus is an extinct genus of aetosaurine aetosaur.

facts.statement: Fossils of Coahomasuchus have been discovered in Texas and North Carolina from Late Triassic deposits dating to the Otischalkian faunachron.
facts.quote: Remains of the genus have been found from deposits in Texas and North Carolina that date to the Otischalkian faunachron (lower late Carnian) of the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Coahomasuchus was small for an aetosaur, measuring less than 1.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: It was small for an aetosaur, being less than 1.5 m long.

facts.statement: The dorsal plates of Coahomasuchus were distinctively flat and unflexed with faint sub-parallel to radial ornamentation.
facts.quote: The dorsal plates are distinctively flat and unflexed, and have a faint sub-parallel to radial ornamentation.

facts.statement: Unlike many other aetosaurs, Coahomasuchus lacked spines or keels on its dorsal plates.
facts.quote: The genus lacked spines or keels on these plates, features seen in many other aetosaurs.

facts.statement: The type species C. kahleorum was named by Heckert and Lucas in 1999.
facts.quote: C. kahleorum, the type species, was named by Heckert and Lucas in 1999

facts.statement: A second species, C. chathamensis, was named by Heckert et al. in 2017 from the Pekin Formation of the Newark Supergroup.
facts.quote: C. chathamensis, a second species named by Heckert et al. in 2017, is from the Pekin Formation of the Newark Supergroup.

facts.statement: The holotype of C. chathamensis includes parts of the skull, a feature that is rare among aetosaurs.
facts.quote: The holotype of the latter species contains parts of the skull, which is rare among aetosaurs.

facts.statement: Coahomasuchus had sharp, recurved teeth indicating a carnivorous diet, a trait shared only with Aetosauroides among aetosaurs.
facts.quote: The teeth were sharp and recurved, indicating a carnivorous diet, a detail only shared with Aetosauroides within aetosauria.

facts.statement: C. chathamensis differs from C. kahleorum by having wider osteoderms on the back and neck underside, as well as different relative lengths of the surangular processes.
facts.quote: C. chathamensis differs from C. kahleorum by wider osteoderms on the back and the underside of the neck, as well as the relative lengths of the processes of the surangular.

facts.statement: Coahomasuchus belongs to the parent group Aetosaurinae.
Coahomasuchus is classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
Coahomasuchus is classified as a reptile.
Coahomasuchus lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Coahomasuchus was very similar in appearance to the closely related genus Aetosaurus.
rejected.quote: Coahomasuchus was very similar in appearance to the closely related Aetosaurus.
